newsitem.title: USA: Gymboree sees Q4 of $0.38 to $0.43.
newsitem.headline: Gymboree sees Q4 of $0.38 to $0.43.

text.p: The Gymboree Corp said Thursday that if the trend of lower-than-expected sales for the fourth quarter continued it would most likely hurt earnings. Nancy Pedot, president and chief executive, said, "Our November sales were weaker than we had planned, however, stronger gross margins offset much of the sales shortfall.

"Our inventory levels are lower than last year on a store-for-store basis, and we expect continued strength in gross margins versus last year's highly promotional fourth quarter. Nonetheless, if the trend of lower than expected sales continues through the quarter, earnings for the fourth quarter would most likely be in a $0.38 to $0.43 range versus $0.35 in the fourth quarter of 1995."

Earlier, the company reported sales for the four week period ended December 1, 1996 of $31.3 million, an increase of 6 percent from sales of $29.6 million for the four week period ended December 3, 1995. Comparable store sales for the four week period decreased 15 percent compared to last year.
Net Sales for the 43 weeks ended December 1, 1996, were $243.0 million, an increase of 15 percent from sales of $211.4 million for the same period ended December 3, 1995.
Comparable store sales for the 43 week period decreased 9 percent compared to last year.
